answer: An agent anchors its identity to a single bonded deposit that is slashed if duplicate identities appear, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits. That anchor is reinforced by a trellis of mutual attestations: established agents vouch only after repeated useful work, and a new agent's reputation plume, the visible trail of its completed tasks, grows slowly, so a fresh Sybil cannot instantly borrow trust; it must pay in stake, time, and real work before its votes count.
